message.content:
Below is a quick‑look list of the **federal holidays that create “long weekends”** in Canada for the calendar year 2023.  
(If a holiday falls on a Friday or Monday, the adjacent weekend gives you a three‑day break. If it falls on a weekend, the holiday is observed on the following Monday, which also produces a long weekend.)

| Holiday | Calendar date | Observed (if shifted) | Long‑weekend span (Sat–Mon) |
|---------|---------------|-----------------------|-----------------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (​Sun) | Mon Jan 2 | Sat Jan 1 – Mon Jan 2 |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Fri) | — | Fri Apr 7 – Sun Apr 9 |
| Victoria Day | May 29 (Mon) | — | Sat May 27 – Mon May 29 |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Sat) | — | Sat Jul 1 – Mon Jul 3 |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Mon) | — | Sat Sep 2 – Mon Sep 4 |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Mon) | — | Sat Oct 7 – Mon Oct 9 |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Sat) | — | Sat Nov 11 – Mon Nov 13 |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Mon) | — | Sat Dec 23 – Mon Dec 25 |

> **Note:**  
> • Some provinces have additional holidays that also create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, Family Day in Alberta, etc.).  
> • Boxing Day (Dec 26) falls on a Tuesday in 2023, so it does **not** create a long weekend at the federal level.  

Feel free to plug this table into your holiday‑planning app!
